originalStatement: For h≥3, E(h)=0 and r=d(h)−1 imply A(v(h))≥r−h and A(r)−A(v(h))≤H(h).

detailedDerivation: Row-sharp follows by counting distinct after-row live values>h: d(h)≥2h+1−A(h). Its lower envelope increases by1 or2 at each step. Equality E(h)=0 therefore forces every later diagonal strictly above d(h)=r+1.

The h−A(h)=r−h old after-row survivors have distinct values in[h+1,r], so they fill that interval. The penultimate y lies there for h≥3 and is not a prior diagonal by the penultimate core lemma. No future owner has value≤r, so y is a blocker.
Each of the r−y higher survivor awards occurs before the last-old y source, forcing y into a distinct older private journal; row injectivity supplies distinct prior service rows with d(t)>y.
All diagonal values≤y have owners<h. Hence the available prior source count is h−R(y)=h−y+A(y), giving A(y)≥r−h.

Because r is below current diagonal, R(r)=h−H(h); therefore A(r)=r−h+H(h), and A(r)−A(y)≤H(h). To conclude y=r one needs both H(h)=0 and r blocker. The general two rank inequalities do not need r to be a blocker.
